scope.summary: Implement BodySpec persistence glue per Section 13.16 (BK-16.3/BK-16.4): storage_glue writes use the event-before-row CTE pattern (ledger event insert and authority row insert in one transaction, event first), and EventLedger replay reconstructs full body authoring state — TAI-OVR-007 parity for bodies: any BodySpec must be rebuildable from its event stream alone.
acceptance_criteria: save_body_spec / save_recipe / record_channel_change write via a single CTE (or transaction) inserting the TAILOR_BODY_* ledger event first and the authority row referencing event_ledger_event_id second; partial failure rolls back both.

replay_body(body_id) folds the ordered tailor.body event stream into a BodySpec; for any body authored through the API, replay output == stored bodykit_bodies row (PartialEq), proven over a scripted authoring sequence.
Replay reports unknown future event types as a typed ReplayWarning (no panic), keeping forward compatibility.
guard_authority_write(AuthorityMode::Postgres) is the first statement of every glue write; no unguarded write path exists (negative test).
scope.risk_if_missed: If body state and the ledger can disagree, recipes stop being reproducible and the operator's saved bodies silently drift — the exact class of unrecoverable state corruption the kernel's event-sourcing law exists to prevent.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
